value.executive_summary: Pass 2 preserves the binding visual thesis — cold system, warm human — while tightening the core daily ritual around state integrity, explicit next-actions, and accessible ceremony. The strongest leverage is to convert transitions into short, deterministic ceremonies that preserve gouache hand-painting, motif frieze, and the game shell, while reducing clutter around decisions. Key opportunities include unifying round/cohort state across journeys, hiding prelaunch themes or rendering placeholders, clarifying primary actions and destinations, rendering essential content by default (motion as enhancement), and hardening the profile two‑step flow with a visible, sticky progression. The binding art direction and warm artefacts remain central; the changes focus on sequencing, feedback clarity, and accessibility to lift completion and daily return rates.

findings.evidence: From 07-advance-4.png: the survival peak shows Rank #7 and a prominent share card, yet there is no explicit tomorrow/daily return anchor visible; the next-day path is not clearly presented on this screen.
findings.journey: Returning player — survival result to next day
findings.rationale: End-of-day ceremony lacks a concrete next-day anchor, weakening intention to return for Day 2.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit Day 2 anchor card beneath the Rank card (e.g., “Day 2 opens at {time}” and a prominent action like “Continue to Day 2”) while keeping share as a secondary option.
findings.user_consequence: Users may feel finished with the day and not primed to return.

findings.evidence: 05-speedrun-beat-1.png shows the check-in panel with a large capture area labeled ‘Snap your proof of presence’ and a dominant red CTA ‘Use a sample shot’, plus a small ‘Or snap your own’ link; beat 3 repeats with no clear progression state.
findings.rationale: Capture flow teaches a shortcut rather than the real gesture; repeated beats lack clear state change between beat 1 and beat 3.
findings.recommendation: Make the capture surface explicitly interactive with a visible pressed state and a secondary Preview/Lock/Retake flow; reposition the primary action so the real gesture (capture) is visually primary over the demo shortcut.
findings.user_consequence: New users may learn a demo path instead of the actual capture gesture.

findings.evidence: 06-speedrun-after-sample.png shows ‘The jury is voting. Your photo is on trial.’ while a voting closed indicator is present, and 07-advance-1.png reaffirms the same 8/2 verdict in the top card.
findings.rationale: Revealing the verdict before the audit removes suspense and harms social tension.
findings.recommendation: Use a sealed, neutral receipt during submission and reveal the Human/Sus counts only after the three peer votes are cast; delay the final verdict until audit-complete.
findings.user_consequence: Audit feels administrative rather than social; suspense is reduced.

findings.evidence: 04-speedrun-day1.png presents Day 1 theme with a strong twist, then a long ‘What counts’ drawer and a five-object motif frieze; the cadence reads as high-load rather than staged ritual.
findings.rationale: The reveal compresses multiple mechanics into a single moment, risking cognitive overload.
findings.recommendation: Split the Day 1 reveal into two states (A: theme/title; B: twist/limits) with a non-autoplay transition, moving the heavier explanations into a dedicated step after the user taps. Keep the frieze as a dwell element but reduce its overlap with the core CTA.
findings.user_consequence: High cognitive load on first reveal may slow onboarding.

findings.evidence: 02-landing-full.png shows long black sections and a dense block labeled ‘HOW IT WORKS’ followed by a blank region before ‘SEE THE LOOP’; reduced-motion states show essential content becoming unreadable.
findings.rationale: Essential headings and loop content should be visible by default to support accessibility and reduce reliance on motion.
findings.recommendation: Render essential headings and loop content by default; apply motion only as enhancement with a motion-ready flag; honor prefers-reduced-motion by showing a complete state without gating content behind animation.
findings.user_consequence: Static content may be unreadable for users with reduced motion or assistive tech limitations.

findings.evidence: Ambient population dots cross CTA zones (01-landing.png) and overlay the theme caption text (03-speedrun-intro.png); in 06-speedrun-after-sample.png, dots obscure percentage labels.
findings.rationale: Ambient layers intrude on precise controls, reducing clarity of decisions.
findings.recommendation: Add ambient masking to keep population dots out of CTA and verdict regions; enforce z-index order ambient < system < human artefact < CTA, and apply pointer-events: none to ambient layers.
findings.user_consequence: Decision areas become visually noisy, decreasing precision and trust.

findings.evidence: GF-09 notes show warm gouache motifs scattered inconsistently (01-landing.png vs 02-landing-full.png vs 05-speedrun-beat-1.png); repeated bus motif appears as a UI glyph rather than a consistent artefact.
findings.rationale: Motif consistency is essential to the game feel; glyphs and emoji-like tokens weaken the hand-painted language.
findings.recommendation: Adopt a single owned motif budget per beat (one painted artefact), remove redundant emoji/glyphs, and apply GouacheFilters consistently across warm artefacts.
findings.user_consequence: Inconsistent warm artefacts dilute the tactile warmth of the world.

findings.evidence: 07-advance-1.png shows human/sus buttons with insufficient spacing and unclear focus state; decorative strings in accessibility tree leak into AT narration.
findings.rationale: Accessibility noise in the audit flow reduces clarity and trust for screen-reader users.
findings.recommendation: Hide decorative strings from AT; ensure proper ARIA labeling for modal and v-dialog interactions; provide a clear focus trap during modal open/close and restore focus to initiating control after close.
findings.user_consequence: Screen-reader users may receive cluttered, non-informative narration.

findings.evidence: 07-advance-4.png shows a warm proof card obscured by a dark overlay; the feast of accents (green, red, yellow) competes for attention.
findings.rationale: Overly busy peak state reduces emphasis on the warm artefact and dilutes the player’s sense of ownership.
findings.recommendation: Lighten the overlay on the share card, maintain warm proof focus, and reserve color encodings for system status (green HUMAN, red SUS) while ensuring a single primary CTA remains dominant.
findings.user_consequence: Warm artefact dominance is weakened, reducing emotional impact of the peak.

findings.evidence: GF-11 notes suggest the share card’s warm artefact should be preserved; current overlay reduces legibility of the proof.
findings.rationale: The shared artefact must be legible during the peak to maintain ritual significance.
findings.recommendation: Render the share card with a warm, legible proof foreground and a restrained trophy chrome; avoid heavy overlays on the image that diminishes warmth.
findings.user_consequence: Share card readability drops, weakening the sense of personal achievement.

interaction_layers_map.ambient: Ambient population field, topographic texture, and decorative motifs that enrich the world without competing with core actions.
interaction_layers_map.cta: Primary controls placed in the lower thumb zone; motion and state changes reinforce progression without clutter.
interaction_layers_map.human: Hand-painted artefacts and motifs (Proof scenes, Mascot, MotifFrieze, ThemeMotif) that carry warmth and personality.
interaction_layers_map.system: Cold, precise chrome for countdowns, votes, pot, and status lines; anchors the ritual to an accountable grid.

mobile_ritual_test_script: 1) Load prelaunch on mobile (320×568, 375×812). Verify prelaunch theme wheel renders placeholders or a noninteractive group; confirm no direct access to individual theme names.
2) Verify the hero’s countdown state transitions when the beta opens (cohort size derived from a single source of truth).
3) On the Reserve flow, ensure single primary action (Reserve) is visually dominant and the speed-run option is clearly secondary.
4) In the profile step, ensure two answers reveal a clearly labeled next action and that the CTA becomes visible within the first viewport or via a sticky footer.
5) Open the spectator/audit path; ensure the audit header theme is consistent with the home state and the briefing modal closes in one step with proper focus restoration.
6) Test reduced-motion: all essential content should be visible with prefers-reduced-motion; verify Escape closes modals and focus returns to the invoking control.
7) Validate empty/locked audit states with a contextual action (Sign in or Retry) and a last-checked time.
8) For returning players, verify the next-action CTA is explicit (e.g., Continue to Day 2) and that sharing remains optional.
9) Run a cold start, warm start, and stale-storage test to confirm state reconciliation and correct first render.
10) Perform automated keyboard and touch regression tests across widths 320–430px with two-answer flows and profile progress.
strengths_to_preserve: The binding art direction (cold system, warm human), gouache motifs, central game shell, hand-painted elements, and warm-ceremony cadence.
The practice entry and threshold feel that stage the ritual rather than present a tool.
The Day 1 theme and its motor/motif (bus, mug) that anchors the day’s warmth.
Audit voting readability in mobile (binary choice layout in thumb zone).
Motif frieze as dwell moments at threshold, waiting, and finale.
The survive/share peak structure that frames post-day outcomes.

top_five_changes.expected_impact: Bind authoritative round/cohort state across journeys; unify state source to a single authoritative object and render reconciliation states.
top_five_changes.implementation_scope: Front-end state model with a single source of truth; add reconciliation checks and a non-conflicting loading/retry UI across Home, Audit, Proof screens.
top_five_changes.title: Bind authoritative round/cohort state across journeys

top_five_changes.expected_impact: Hide prelaunch themes with placeholders until reveal to preserve the ritual mystery and prevent full disclosure.
top_five_changes.implementation_scope: UI path for prelaunch with placeholders or a noninteractive wheel; accessible semantics for hidden state.
top_five_changes.title: Conceal prelaunch themes with placeholders until reveal

top_five_changes.expected_impact: Clarify primary-action hierarchy and destinations to reduce mobile friction.
top_five_changes.implementation_scope: Relabel CTAs to explicit destinations; collapse competing primary actions; ensure downstream navigation is visible in first viewport or via sticky footer.
top_five_changes.title: Clarify action destinations and reduce competing primary paths

top_five_changes.expected_impact: Render essential content by default; move motion to enhancement only.
top_five_changes.implementation_scope: CSS/markup changes to remove initial opacity gating; add motion-ready class; honor reduced-motion across major screens.
top_five_changes.title: Make essential content visible by default (motion as enhancement)

top_five_changes.expected_impact: Harden profile progression with a sticky footer and explicit progression.
top_five_changes.implementation_scope: UI footer, visible progress indicator, and focus/scroll management; regression tests across mobile widths.
top_five_changes.title: Harden profile progression with sticky footer and destination labels

unresolved_questions: What is the authoritative beta cohort size and payout model for production (25 vs 50; automatic vs manual payout)?
Are prelaunch themes truly intended to be hidden in all states, or is the exposure a temporary artifact during a buggy prelaunch state?
Is the two-step day briefing modality intentional, or should it be collapsed into a single-step flow?
Should spectators be allowed to vote before slot reservation is paid, or is voting gatekeeper tied strictly to an active cohort?
What exact copy and data source should drive reward bonuses (the roadmap vs UI text), and how will this be validated in beta?
How should the accessibility tree handle decorative background strings to avoid exposing non-informative language to ATs?
Is the two-answer CTA behavior a regression or a deliberate product decision, and how should regression testing be structured to catch reoccurrence?
